The paper studies electromagnetic scattering for time-domain Maxwell's equations in an unbounded structure.
The structure is an infinite rough surface, a non-local perturbation of an infinite plane surface.
The usual Silver–Mueller radiation condition is not valid for unbounded structures.
An exact time-domain transparent boundary condition (TBC) is developed.
The scattering problem is reformulated as an initial-boundary value problem in an infinite rectangular slab.
The well-posedness and stability of the reduced problem are established.
The method of energy, the Lax–Milgram lemma, and the inversion theorem of the Laplace transform are used.
A priori estimates with explicit time dependence are derived for the electric field.
The dielectric permittivity and magnetic permeability are assumed to be real, bounded, and measurable functions.
The initial conditions for the electric and magnetic fields are compactly supported in the infinite rectangular slab.
Sobolev spaces H(curl,Ω) and H0(curl,Ω) are used for the functional spaces.
Tangential functional spaces H−1/2(curl,Γj) and H−1/2(div,Γj) are introduced for the boundary conditions.
The Laplace transform is used to derive the transparent boundary condition.
The capacity operator B j is continuous and maps H−1/2(curl,Γj) to H−1/2(div,Γj).
The real part of the sesquilinear form involving B j is non-negative.
The paper provides a rigorous mathematical foundation for the analysis of electromagnetic scattering in unbounded structures.
The results are relevant for applications in radar, optics, and geophysics.
The assumptions are restrictive for the dielectric permittivity and magnetic permeability.
Future research directions include finding the least restrictive conditions for the coefficients.
The paper is organized into sections on problem formulation, auxiliary problems, well-posedness, and conclusions.
